name: midasmlpy
what_it_holds: Python port of the midasml approach: regularized MIDAS regression using orthogonal-polynomial (Legendre) weighting plus sparse-group LASSO, fast proximal block-coordinate-descent solver, tools for high-dimensional mixed-frequency panel data. Sibling implementations exist in R, Julia, MATLAB. 151 commits, GPL-2.0, last updated 2025-05-15 (33 stars).
why_useful: High-dimensional MIDAS with regularization is well suited to nowcasting a quarterly ABNB KPI from many weekly/daily alt-data series (Trends, calendar pace, reviews index, FX) without manual factor selection.
themes: Nowcasting methods and packages: MIDAS, dynamic factor models, bridge equations, nowcasting with Google Trends, KPI nowcasting for companies

name: midasr

Includes a /data folder with bundled example mixed-frequency datasets. 522 commits.
why_useful: Most mature, citable MIDAS implementation (basis for many derivative packages found this pass); quantile-MIDAS (midas_qr) is a route to nowcasting a distribution/range for ABNB nights or ADR rather than a point estimate.

why_all: The Monash Time Series Forecasting Archive (github.com/rakshitha123/TSForecasting is the code/loader repo, data lives on Zenodo) is the standard reference tourism benchmark used across the forecasting-ML literature; CC-BY-4.0 licensed and machine-loadable via the .tsf reader in the GitHub repo, useful if the team wants a clean point-forecast-accuracy backtesting harness comparable to published tourism-forecasting baselines (gap #17).

name: GTFS-ride
what_it_holds: 52-star, Apache-2.0 open standard/spec (with reference tooling) for storing and sharing fixed-route transit ridership data alongside GTFS static/realtime feeds; maintained by Oregon DOT's Public Transit Section.
why_useful: A standardized schema/tooling layer that many US transit agencies (and some international) increasingly publish ridership in; useful as a discovery/normalization method for pulling ridership from agencies beyond MTA/TfL/RATP without bespoke parsers.
themes: Public transit ridership and airport rail links (MTA, TfL, RATP, JR) as visitor proxies; ridership open data
why_all: A standardized schema/tooling layer that many US transit agencies (and some international) increasingly publish ridership in; useful as a discovery/normalization method for pulling ridership from agencies beyond MTA/TfL/RATP without bespoke parsers.
